 Intense love and betrayal expected in Disney+ K-drama ‘The Remarried Empress’
 Josiah Antonio - The Philippine Star November 8, 2026 | 12:00am 
 Shin Min-a plays Navier, the empress of the Eastern Empire, whose marriage and position are threatened when her husband decides to take a mistress. Photos courtesy of Disney+ Philippines 
 MANILA, Philippines — Viewers are expected to experience intense scenes of love and betrayal in the new Disney+ Korean series “The Remarried Empress.”
 The K-drama started airing this week, but ahead of its premiere, The Philippine STAR, along with other select media, had the opportunity to watch its first two episodes, and here’s what we know about it so far.
 The series, based on the web novel of the same name, also has a Philippine trailer and a teleserye original soundtrack or OST, Till I Met You, sung by “Tawag Ng Tanghalan Duets” winner Marielle Montellano.
 In its pilot episode, we are introduced to the royal couple Navier (Shin Min-a) and Sovieshu (Ju Ji-hoon), who are navigating their lives, particularly how to finally bear a child in order to have an heir to the throne of the Eastern Empire.
 Ju Ji-hoon portrays Sovieshu, the emperor of the Eastern Empire, whose decision to bring another woman into his life puts his marriage to Navier at risk. 
 For several years, other relatives have attempted to snatch the crown from them as they stay in power.
 During a bow hunt, Sovieshu meets Rashta (Lee Se-young), a victim of abuse by several men.
 Sovieshu becomes like Rashta’s knight in shining armor as he saves the runaway slave from harm.
 He decides to keep this a secret from Navier as he develops special feelings for the rescued woman and tries to elevate her status.
 Elsewhere in the Eastern Empire’s forest, Navier finds herself in trouble and meets a mysterious bird. She manages to escape danger, but the incident leaves her with more questions than answers.
 Lee Se-young takes on the role of Rashta, a runaway slave whose life changes after she meets Emperor Sovieshu and becomes his mistress. 
 As they return to the palace, the empress becomes skeptical of her husband and confronts him about what really happened in the forest.
 Sovieshu eventually admits that he met Rashta and wants her to become his legal mistress, but the empress refuses.
 Navier is devastated by the recent development as she continues to hope that she will have a child with Sovieshu.
 Meanwhile, the mysterious bird she encountered in the forest reappears with a message, introducing the empress to a secret pen pal.
 However, she remains troubled by her husband’s request. And to her surprise, Albani (Jung Young-joo), who is also seeking the throne, adopts Rashta so that she can legally become a mistress.
 Navier concedes to Sovieshu’s wish, and the latter pampers Rashta with all the love he thinks she deserves as his new lover.
 Lee Jong-seok plays Heinrey, the prince of the Western Empire, who forms an unlikely alliance with Navier as she deals with the challenges in her marriage and royal life. 
 As she feels lost in love, Navier continues to communicate with the bird, but she is also determined to seek revenge against her ex-husband and overpower him.
 In the coming episodes, viewers will witness Navier form an unlikely alliancewith Heinrey (Lee Jong-seok) of the Western Empire as they challenge Sovieshu.
 As she attempts to reclaim what’s hers, Navier will explore her relationship with the prince of the Western Empire while figuring out how she will be able to get what she deserves.
 “The Remarried Empress” registered a strong debut on Disney+, becoming the streaming platform’s most-viewed local original premiere of all time globally, including Hulu, based on its first three days of release.
 According to Disney, the Korean fantasy romance also recorded the biggest premiere for a Korean title in more than 50 markets worldwide, including the US, UK, Canada, France, Germany, Spain, Mexico, Chile, Australia and New Zealand.
 New episodes of the K-drama series “The Remarried Empress” drop every Wednesday on Disney+.
